title: X marks a clip, and Shift I and Shift O go to the marks, as in Premiere
goal: Premiere editors mark a whole clip with X and jump to their In and Out with Shift I and Shift O. Here X does not mark a clip and Shift I and Shift O do nothing on the timeline, so marking a clip to lift or extract it takes two trips with the playhead. Give the timeline these three keys.
notes:
Key map: Sources/PhotonzCore/TimelineKeys.swift ~153-233 (pure, test-first in PhotonzCoreTests); dispatch in Sources/Photonz/EditorState+TimelineKeys.swift ~289, which takes presses before the menu bar while the timeline has the keyboard. X today is the fill swap on an invisible tool bar stand-in that answers under every tool (EditorCommands.swift ~140): make sure the timeline's X wins only while the timeline holds the keyboard. Option X (Clear In and Out) already exists (EditorCommands.swift ~888, TimelineMenuKeys.clearInOut) and should sit beside the new rows. Marks and extract: the done task marking-an-in-and-an-out-and-pressing-one-key-ta.

Found by the Premiere key gap check this pass: X, Shift I, Shift O missing, no task or card covers or declined them (searched mark clip, go to in, shift i).
acceptance: With the timeline holding the keyboard, X sets In and Out to the start and end of the clip under the playhead (the topmost picture track's clip there), and Command Z takes the marks back
Shift I moves the playhead to the In mark and Shift O to the Out mark; with no mark set they do nothing and say nothing
After a click on the picture, X keeps its Photoshop meaning (swap the fill colours), the same rule M, I and O already follow
Sequence shows rows for Mark Clip, Go to In and Go to Out with these keys

Ships at Next defaults; the try path is: open a recording, press B at two and at four seconds, put the playhead at three seconds, press X, then apostrophe to extract the clip; then mark again and press Shift I and Shift O

audit written under queue/audits/ and the keys added to docs/design/video-vs-premiere.md, and anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar and written into this task log if it does not

log.note: adversarial review before: a Premiere editor presses X expecting the clip under the playhead marked; here B/Cmd K cut a clip into pieces of one layer, so X marks the PIECE under the playhead (what Premiere does after a razor cut, since each piece is its own clip there). No track targeting here, so: the picked clip under the playhead, else the topmost picture, else the topmost sound (a sound layer added later sits above the picture in layer order, and should not win). Collision: X is the fill swap on an invisible tool bar stand-in; the timeline router takes the press first only while it holds the keyboard, and with nothing under the playhead X is still kept by the timeline so it never swaps fills behind a person's back. No mock draws these; keys + Sequence rows only.

review after, on the probe: x-marks-the-clip-walk (no flags, no front) passes: X at 3s marks 2000-4000 on the cuts, Cmd Z takes both marks back in one step, apostrophe extracts to 6s, Shift I/Shift O go to the marks, nothing moves with no marks, five X presses on the timeline never swapped fills, one after a click on the picture did (#000000 -> #FFFFFF in log). mark-clip-menu-rows-walk passes: Sequence reads Mark Clip X, Go to In ⇧I, Go to Out ⇧O (dimmed with nothing marked), one key each. Neighbour walks fill-colours-say-themselves, premiere-keys-on-the-timeline and extract-a-marked-stretch green. Shift O on an Out at the very end lands on the last frame (scrub clamps), which is Premiere's behaviour too. left rough, not filed (no person-visible defect): Mark Clip is not on the clip or ruler right-click menus; Premiere's clip menu has no Mark Clip either.

X marks the piece under the playhead (picked clip there, else topmost picture, else topmost sound) while the timeline holds the keyboard, one undo step; Shift I / Shift O go to the In / Out, nothing with no mark; after a click on the picture X swaps fills again.
